newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle departs Russia's Mir.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle departs Russia's Mir.

text.p: The space shuttle Atlantis uncoupled from Russia's Mir space station on Wednesday, leaving behind NASA astronaut Michael Foale and tonnes of supplies and equipment
Atlantis slipped the metallic grip of Mir's docking port at 9:04 p.m. EDT (0104 GMT) as the two craft soared into the sunrise 245 miles (395 km) above the planet.
"Houston, we have separation," shuttle skipper Charles Precourt radioed mission control as four springs gently nudged the Atlantis away from Mir.

The shuttle left behind British-born astronaut Michael Foale for a four-month tour of duty aboard the Russian orbital outpost. Foale replaces NASA astronaut Jerry Linenger, who has lived and worked aboard the station since January.
Linenger and six crewmates are to return to Earth aboard Atlantis on Saturday. The shuttle was making its sixth visit to the space station.

Atlantis also delivered a record 4,000 lbs (1,814 kg) of supplies and equipment to Mir, including a new device for generating breathing oxygen and repair gear to plug leaks in the station's cooling systems.
